### Observed differences

- The execution order between two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, A26 ran before A35, A36 and A41 in about 99–100 in 100 traces, and A27 ran before them in about 98–100 in 100. In the later window this is inverted: A35, A36 and A41 run before A26 in about 99–100 in 100 traces and before A27 in about 98–99 in 100. Each pair still occurs together in essentially every trace in both windows, so participation itself did not change. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Event positions moved consistently with the reversal: the mean relative position of A35, A36 and A41 moved earlier, from about 0.58–0.59 of the trace to about 0.41, while A26 moved later (about 0.53 to 0.62) and A27 moved later (about 0.38 to 0.47). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Successor choices around these groups changed in the same direction. A25 earlier led almost exclusively to A27 (about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions); in the later window it leads to A35, A36 and A41 in roughly equal thirds. A26 earlier fed into A41, A35 and A36 (about 37%, 34% and 28%); in the later window it leads almost always to A30 (about 99 in 100). A35, A36 and A41 each earlier passed to A30 about 28–37% of the time; in the later window that edge has nearly vanished (about 1 in 200) and each instead passes to A27 about 29–34% of the time. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a re-sequencing hypothesis: the group A35, A36, A41, which in the earlier window ran after A26 and A27 in nearly every trace, runs before them in the later window, while A27 and A30 exchange roles around this group — A27, previously entered from A25 ahead of the group, is now handed over to by A35, A36 and A41 (about 29–34% of each one's transitions), and A30, previously reached from those three activities, is now reached almost directly from A26 (about 99 in 100 of A26's transitions). A25 correspondingly now enters the group directly instead of leading to A27. The order reversal is near-deterministic in both windows, the position shifts of all five activities point the same way, and the successor redistributions at A25, A26, A35, A36 and A41 all match the same movement; in total 16 control-flow items qualified, roughly 30 times the about 0.5 expected if nothing had changed. Participation is unchanged — each of the five activities occurs in essentially every trace in both windows — so this is a change in ordering and placement, not activities becoming optional or one path replacing another. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

The DIR, POS and REL items plausibly describe one underlying re-sequencing rather than independent confirmations, and the exact resulting sequence is only partly determined: A27's own outgoing transitions were not profiled (the DIR sources are A25, A26, A35, A36 and A41) and no step-distance items are present, so the placement of A27 relative to A26 after the group is inferred indirectly. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the later window is dominated by a pre-existing opposite-order variant that was too rare to appear in the earlier sample (about 0–1 in 100 traces) and now accounts for about 99 in 100, rather than a single flow having been re-sequenced. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

Other differences: none beyond low-frequency successor noise — a few new outgoing transitions from A25, A26, A35, A36 and A41, each carrying about 1 in 200 of that source's transitions in the later window. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
